question.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
question.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ -5 & 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ -5 & 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}7 & -5 \\ -5 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(49-25) \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$
